text: Good evening. This is Global Observer. Polls have just closed in Meridia, and the first official count is coming in.
The national electoral commission reports turnout of seventy-one per cent, the highest since the country's first multiparty vote in two thousand and four.
With sixty per cent of districts counted, the opposition Coastal Alliance leads on forty-four per cent. The governing Unity Party follows on thirty-eight.
The swing is sharpest in the northern highlands, where three districts have changed hands for the first time.
The commission expects final results within forty-eight hours. International observers will publish their first assessment tomorrow.
What to watch: whether the Alliance crosses fifty per cent, or a coalition decides who governs. This is Global Observer.
